$description: The bar across the top of the Project Styles canvas: the filter that narrows the specimen catalogue, and the toggle that reduces it to the elements this file has already styled. Both are shell state rather than document state — the adapter owns which — and the two names come in as values, because the surface is called Project Styles and the canvas view it draws is the wire word `stylebook`; nothing a reader sees here may be spelled from that. **The bar IS the kit's toolbar now.** It used to write `role="toolbar"` and its own `aria-label` on a `<div>`, which is a role with none of the behaviour under it: two controls, two tab stops, and no arrow key between them. `jx-action-group` is not the element for it — that one roves `jx-action-button` and this bar's first control is a `jx-textfield` — so `jx-toolbar` is, and the field keeps its own arrows while its caret still has text to walk (ui.md §5.5).

style.$description: What `.sb-chrome` said in `styles/overlays.css`, plus the six inline declarations the template carried beside it, plus `.tb-toggle` — all three go dead with this conversion, and none of them is shared with another surface. Three repairs on the way. The bar is one element rather than a positioned box wrapping a `role="toolbar"` row that declared the same flex layout again. The flex layout is not declared here EITHER any more: `display: flex`, `align-items: center`, the `--jx-space-2` gap, the sans face and the foreground colour are all `jx-toolbar`'s own, so what is left below is only what a positioned BAND is. And `.tb-toggle` read `var(--spectrum-font-size-50, 11px)`, which the kit spells `--jx-text-sm` at the same value; the rest of its drawing is a `jx-action-button` reaching in through `part="control"`, because what it has to look like is a small bordered chip and every fill and control height the kit draws would otherwise have to be taken back off.

& [part=\"customized\"] > [part=\"contro.$description: Bordered, unfilled and dimmed until it is on, which is what says it is a filter rather than an action: the catalogue it narrows is the thing the reader is looking at, so the control has to be quieter than its subject.

& [part=\"customized\"][data-selected] >.$description: `data-selected` and not `selected`: the kit reflects the pressed state as a data attribute (`jx-action-button.json`), and the property this document binds never reaches the attribute of the same name.

children.$description: `onchange` and not `onclick`: a `toggles` button owns its own pressed state and says so with `change` (`jx-action-button.json`), and an `onclick` written here would replace the element's own click handler on the same property — the toggle would stop flipping and stop announcing `aria-pressed`.
